17 October2026 · implementation and repeated native review · working tree uncommitted

Usability fixes across Mac, iPhone and iPad

Repeated source review, regression tests and fresh native screenshots caught and corrected further issues. This report does not claim that the product has no usability problems. Unverified interactions and remaining design tradeoffs are listed explicitly.

Original comprehensive audit and competitor evidence

What changed

Editor and precision

Bounded higher-detail zoom; explicit Pan mode; fractional brush size entry; visible Auto Sample/Sampled state; safe Retouch Before/After; current-input preview guards; Retry and source recovery; adaptive large-text controls; one Undo per numeric edit; clearer tool/reset/compare labels.

Filters and sizing

Candidate tiles retained across intensity changes; one filter browser; Original disables irrelevant removal; percentage entry; Fit preset labels and sizing consequences; common portrait crop ratios.

Workspace and scope

All visibility predicates clear together without clearing selection; active filter count; explicit photo counts; contextual task and capacity labels; Resize in Actions; workspace framing reset excludes hidden retained creation sources.

Removal and projects

Session-local Undo Remove restores membership, tabs, favourites and selection without replacing edits or expanding a newly captured batch. Cleanup protects Undo sources; saved instructions omit Undo-only ownership. Project switches expire that ownership before saving the previous project.

Output and import

New outcome feedback survives old export cards; reviewed files have identities; Photos saving is single-flight and tracks partial success for retry; recognized picker cancellation remains quiet; original files remain protected.

GIFs

Explicit active-frame and selected-group actions; mixed timing; annotation visibility descriptions; grouped field Undo including pending edits; saved creation access and empty submenu fix; filenames and unrelated imports no longer rebuild previews.

Collages

Saved-name search; useful empty states; local selection filters and Files import; bounded source recovery with specific reference recovery; visible movement mode and separate nondestructive View Zoom; no changed crop gesture semantics.

Mac Automations

A coherent local draft with Cancel or Cancel & Resume and Save & Keep Paused; atomic persistence before commit; live job state retained; editing suspends monitoring; jobs show filenames and actions explain their scope.

Native test harness

The Mac InvalidTransition failure was traced to a forbidden fixed screenshot dump, not assumed to be a renderer defect. Removing that redundant dump preserves XCTAttachments and allows the full long native test to pass.

Full-platform tests build the Mac and iOS application targets. Native hosted fixtures exercise errors, recovery, saved creations, compact layouts and large text. Final focused reruns cover the last compact-toolbar UI change. Two simulator skips: permission-dependent Photos integration and hardware-specific release performance. Earlier failed runs are retained as evidence; assertions were not weakened.

Fresh native captures

The same bundled demo workspace is used across platforms. Click a screenshot to enlarge. Portrait photos retain their aspect ratio; neutral margins are intentional and are not removed by cropping the photo.

Remaining checks and tradeoffs

Hands-on gestures and assistive technology

Native hosted layout tests cover compact, landscape and accessibility sizes. They do not prove Pencil/finger arbitration, true multi-touch, VoiceOver traversal, Switch Control or external-keyboard feel. The Device Hub UI exposed no usable window in this session, so direct interactive verification is limited.

Performance and visual quality

No M1 8GB release performance certification or physical-device memory-pressure measurement was completed. Detail renders are bounded at3200px, not a full-resolution region-of-interest brush engine. Heal texture choice still needs real photographic stroke comparisons; it cannot be promised flawless.

Further design refinement

Floating panels remain edge-docked rather than vertically anchored to every tool icon. Saved GIF selection remains a named menu rather than a visual browser. Draft tools intentionally retain Apply/Cancel safety while ordinary adjustments commit immediately. These remain reviewable usability tradeoffs, not declared solved.

Release and system integration

Photos add-only permission integration and opt-in release performance tests are skipped. Public support/privacy URLs and signed distribution artifacts remain submission blockers. Simulator success is not physical-device verification.

Competitive principles retained

Keep the canvas dominant, expose one current tool and its contextual controls, separate view zoom from editing geometry, and progressively disclose detailed settings. This follows the documented division between tools, contextual options and panels in Photoshop for iPad and Affinity Photo2 for iPad. Apple describes Photomator as a fast photo-editing and batch workflow. These are design references, not evidence that Ameluma matches their polish or that their current apps were tested here.

No commit, push, publication or signing changes were made during this pass.
